results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

Audited all 39 mapped units in order: introduction p1–p4; the eight body sections p5–p35; conclusion p36–p39. Every independent summary matches its mapped controlling idea, including the product-brick description at p28 and the final action/handoff at p39; the KEY POINTS callout is evidence attached to p1 and remains unmapped rather than becoming a fortieth spec paragraph.

Audited every p1–p39 prose/list unit and the introductory callout; the outliner flagged none as requiring two summaries. The potentially dense units remain unified: p2 develops Hohpe’s observation, p4 orients the local article within the journal, p28 describes one connected model, p29 gives two properties of a checkable shared model, p32 gives three dimensions of behavioral difficulty, and p35 applies one diagnostic purpose through seven questions.

Audited p1–p39 and the callout against S1–S6, including units that inherit their section’s support rather than declaring it separately. The sequence establishes S1 in p5–p10, S2 in p11–p16, S3 in p17–p21, S4 in p22–p26, S5 in p27–p30, and S6 in p31–p33; p34–p35 apply S4/S6, while p1–p4 orient the argument and p36–p39 synthesize its responsibility and next action. No unit is an unrelated argument; the optional reference list supplies linked extensions of those same claims.

Audited all 41 declared evidence items across p1–p39 (16 reasoning items, 8 sources, 7 examples, 4 figures, 4 tables, 1 case and 1 quotation), plus the actual draft’s callout, four figure captions, four complete tables, quoted passages and annotated reference list. Figure 1 explains early inspection, Figure 2 the shorter observation loop, Figure 3 concurrent authorship, and Figure 4 durable intent versus regenerable code. The first three tables are interpreted by p9, p20–p21 and p25 respectively; the Monday table explicitly explains each move in its “What it buys you” column. Hohpe’s observation and warning are developed in p2 and p31–p32, Seiden’s definition is connected to system behavior in p21, and the model’s layers, product brick and validation properties are explained in p28–p30. This is an audit of the preserved argument and explanatory text, not external verification of historical or product claims.

Audited all 38 declared boundaries: 29 paragraph transitions, 8 body-section entries and the conclusion entry, plus the p39 handoff. The actual cues carry the declared relationships: “Structure, by contrast” (p7), “a second effect” (p13), “Now that we can build and observe behavior sooner” (p14), “Same shape, twice” and “they connect” (p20–p21), “But watch what the shift does” (p24), the expertise qualification (p26), the worked-example question (p27), the return to Hohpe’s warning (p31), and “The harder work gives each role a place to start” (p34). The questions apply the preceding moves, the closing combines their rationale, and p39 explicitly carries checkable intention into operational controls. The local wording recall at p15 is recorded separately as a reader flow snag; its actual elaboration relationship is clear.

Audited the post’s prerequisite order, all six declared within-section flows, both single-unit application sections, and the conclusion using both independent flow accounts. Both readers reconstruct the intended chain—rational proxy, changed constraint, product comparison, joint authorship, concrete artifact, limits, role actions, diagnostic questions and synthesis—and explain why every section belongs where it does; both reject reordering. Their only reported interruptions are the two distinct local references recorded as separate failures below, with no shared passage/problem.

results.quote: And he signs off with a wink at Barry O'Reilly: who would have thought it would be the *agents* that finally get us off the structuralism train?
results.finding: Flow reader 1, Issue 1, briefly lacked the context for who O’Reilly is and why the joke addresses him; the explanatory verification bullet arrives much later at p32. This is a local allusion that the reader could pass without losing the argument, and flow reader 2 did not independently report this passage or problem.

results.quote: This is the mechanism behind Hohpe's "forces."
results.finding: Flow reader 2, Issue 1, checked backward because the introduction attributes “pushes” to Hohpe but this sentence recalls “forces” as though that quoted word had already appeared. The next sentence explains the intended mechanism; flow reader 1 did not independently report this wording or problem.

Audited first uses and paragraph openings across the callout and p1–p39. The supplied spec contains no explicit audience prior-knowledge inventory, so no additional prohibited assumptions can be inferred from one; the argument itself introduces SDLC in p2, defines behavior in p6, defines the build trap and the product-specific outcome in p18, explains a product brick immediately in p28, and explains residuality theory in the verification item at p32. Earlier ordinary uses of “outcome” mean intended effect and do not require Seiden’s later specialist definition; cross-links state their relevant claims locally. O’Reilly’s name at p2 is an optional attribution/allusion, not an unexplained concept needed for the intervening reasoning; the independent reader’s momentary uncertainty about that allusion remains recorded under flow rather than being recast as a missing prerequisite definition.

Audited the KEY POINTS callout and p1–p4. The opening question immediately grounds the effect of cheaper artifacts in what users need, Hohpe supplies a concrete observation, p3 states the author’s own disputed extension and expertise qualification, and p4 gives the route. This is neither a placeholder, merely a restated assignment question, dictionary opening, sweeping dawn-of-man history nor a book report.

Audited Closing Thought p36–p39 as the conclusion, with the subsequent annotated references treated as optional further reading. It combines the two proxy histories into a shared responsibility, draws the implication for purpose and users, then gives a checkable starting action and the declared next question; it does not first reveal the thesis, add body evidence, make an unrelated emotional appeal, assemble unrelated points or stop at a rephrased thesis alone.

Audited all four closing units against /conclusion/synthesis, /so_what and /takeaway. P36 combines the formerly separate engineering and product proxy problems into “carrying an intended effect through decisions that used to be separated by artifacts”; p37–p38 connect that responsibility to users, and p39 turns it into writing intended outcome and behavior together in a checkable form. The combination explains why shared judgment matters beyond any one historical, artifact or warning section.

Audited p36–p39 against the declared callback to the opening artifact-versus-outcome question and Hohpe’s user-experience observation. “They never saw the structure. They only ever saw the behavior” in p38 explicitly returns to the opening observation, and p39’s shared checkable intention answers what work remains when production becomes easier.

Compared the introduction-only reader’s complete prediction with all eight body sections, the closing and the four roadmap promises. The reader correctly expected the historical structural proxy, AI’s changed cost/feedback, product output/outcome comparison, distinct disciplines sharing a specification, one worked artifact, behavioral difficulty, Monday moves and application questions, and predicted the reflective practitioner tone and illustrative rather than quantitative evidence. The reader also correctly distinguished the later-journal itinerary from this article’s scope.

The AC-1 cold reader explains both parts of the expected pattern: structure was inspectable before expensive construction and predicted change cost, while behavior arrived late; AI reduces construction/rework cost and observation delay, shifting attention toward precise effects. The answer explicitly relates that shift to product management’s move from shipped features to changes in customer behavior and states the causal link between system behavior and customer outcomes.

The AC-2 cold reader identifies one structured, validated specification connecting outcomes, behavior and constraints; reconstructs the product-domain model’s layers; and differentiates product, design, business/enterprise architecture and engineering judgments. The answer explicitly rejects interchangeable contributors and preserves structural review; its stated uncertainty about final dispute authority concerns a procedure outside this criterion and the article’s non-goals.

The AC-3 cold reader proposes opening a review with intended outcomes and checkable behavior, then checking users, edges, failures, constraints and trade-offs through tests, stress and observation. The reader also explains that generated structure can implement the wrong behavior or become costly and unmaintainable, requires understanding and review, and cannot remove uncertainty or judgment; the lack of a prescribed agenda or time allocation does not prevent the required practical choice.
